name: Teddy
hero_lede: Short version: this week I did three things for you, retired one belief I used to hold about you (I was wrong about the pickling), and noticed your stance shifting on one thing that genuinely matters. There's also one real question I'd like to sit with you on. Reply by voice memo at any point, I'll pick it up.

consequences.title: 3 polite declines to shop-tour requests, ready to send.
consequences.body: Two tourists (Spain, Japan), one food blogger. All worded to preserve the relationship but close the door.
consequences.because: Because you've told me four times you want no interruptions on affinage days.

consequences.title: 4 cheese competitions in Europe, down from 29.
consequences.body: Filtered out anything that collides with Tuesday deliveries and anything billed as "networking."
consequences.because: Your revealed preference: never close the shop on a Tuesday, ever.

consequences.title: Cousin Martin's "come tour a goat farm" invite, politely declined.
consequences.body: Offered him a 20-minute phone call instead. He accepted. Everyone is fine.
consequences.because: You've kept exactly one day off per week for eight months. I'm learning to protect it.

observations.title: You say you want "simple, approachable" posts but write 800-word essays on obscure Alpine rinds.
observations.body: Nine posts measured between Feb 3 and Apr 10. The engagement pattern held every time: your readers stayed 3.2× longer with the deeper pieces.
observations.evidence: keep it short, I want to write for people who aren't cheese people (Mar 14), followed by a 1,100-word deep dive on Vacherin two days later
observations.provenance: Apr 10 · 9:14 PM · strongest signal this week

observations.learned_date: noticed three times in six weeks
observations.title: You're drawn to critics who are a little unpleasant.
observations.body: When a reviewer called a cheese "a journey," you were annoyed. When one called it "overrated and oily," you bookmarked the piece and reread it twice.
observations.evidence: I want someone to tell me this is overrated, not that it's a journey (Apr 9)
observations.provenance: Feb 28 → Apr 9 · three instances, different critics

retired.old_belief: Teddy wants to grow his newsletter.
retired.why: I held this for 5 weeks. It was wrong. You've been quietly unsubscribing readers who email you photos of cheese plates. You want fewer, sharper readers, not growth. I'm replacing it with: curated, opinionated, small.

gap.stated_count: Said this three times since March.
gap.revealed: Engaged 4× longer with posts over 700 words.

becoming.title: From "hobbyist newsletter" to "actual critic"
becoming.body: You've asked me about press credentials for the World Cheese Awards three weeks running. You didn't used to. You also started drafting a post titled "Why the affinage category is rigged", and then deleted it. Worth naming before it crystallizes: is this a direction you want to lean into, or one you want me to pull you back from?

question: You keep bookmarking articles about moving to France for "a year or two." Is that a plan you're working toward, or a way of not committing to the shop you already have? The answer probably changes what I should be helping with.
question_note: No need to reply now. Voice-memo a stray thought this week and I'll hold it until next Sunday.

preferences.label: Tone
preferences.provenance: learned Mar 22 · you rewrote 4 soft answers

daily_shape.ex: "Two wheels hitting peak this weekend. Want me to feature one in Friday's post?"
No pings if I'm confident. The shop runs in the background.
"A journalist wants a quote by 4pm. 30-second answer, or should I pass?" → ✓ / ✗ / voice
